第781章 内部归因与外部归因（第1页）
“我们先从内部说起。”林恩整理着思路，指尖轻轻敲击着桌面，“假设亚空间能影响现实，催生出怪物、恶魔这类东西，其根源往往是欲望与恶念。”
“那么世界本身，按理说应该存在一种动态平衡。由欲望产生的‘恶’，在得到满足后，其力量理应减弱——即便是贪婪，过度膨胀后也会引发反噬，让周围人厌恶、对抗，从而形成制衡。”
他顿了顿，看向莉雅：“比如说，性欲你知道吧？”
莉雅耳尖微红，轻轻点了点头：“嗯，知道。”
“你问这个……做什么？”她双手不自觉地交握，显得有些局促。
“色欲，也就是性欲，当它被满足后，其驱动力应当减弱，因为需求已经暂时平息。”
“暴怒也是一样。当脾气发泄出去后，人的情绪会得到释放，心情反而会平复不少，耐心也会随之回升。”
林恩话锋一转，目光变得锐利：“那么，在一种只有内部归因，完全排除外部归因的环境下，会发生什么？”
“任何事情出了问题，都只怀疑自己？”莉雅睁大了眼睛，仿佛瞬间触及了某个一直被她忽略的盲区。
“没错。”林恩的指尖在桌面上敲出清晰的节奏，“任何事情都归咎于自身，甚至世界‘病’了，人们还在怀疑是不是自己的问题，从而陷入无止境的内耗。”
“但如果始终找不到真正的原因呢？如果现有的‘治疗方法’完全无效呢？”
“那是不是……就该考虑外部归因了？”
“也就是说，和我们目前调查得出的逻辑与结论，完全吻合。”
他身体微微前倾，注视着莉雅的眼睛：
“那些看起来、听起来都和你一样的人……可能根本不是人。而是像‘兽人’那样的存在——它们从灵魂结构上就与你完全不同。”
“可如果你认为‘大家都一样’，只是把它看作单纯的‘恶人’，那么你怀疑的是什么？”
“你怀疑的，依然只是同一个种族内部的问题。”

“把这个逻辑放大到世界层面，也是一样。假设世界真的存在‘情绪影响现实’的法则——”
“那么，当所有人都认为‘是自己的错导致了这一切’，那个故意制造这种矛盾的种族、个体，或者某种意志……它能从中得到什么？”
而受害者完全意识不到问题出在外部，反而不断自责，认为一切都是自己的过错。”
“也就是说……从你的那个梦，以及我这套推演来看，我们是不是该重新审视——深渊族的‘异族’身份，可能远比我们想象的更加‘异质’？”
“然后，是神明，莉雅。”他回想起那些记载中的神只，“你说过，神明本是概念的化身，其权柄也与概念紧密相连。”
“可如果那个概念本身被污染、扭曲了呢？邪神，不就是这样诞生的吗？”
至少，那位“爱神”的堕落，似乎就是如此。
“莉雅，你说……”林恩抛出了一个试探性的问题，目光却深邃地观察着她的反应，“假如一位神明想要‘恢复正常’，祂应该怎么做？”
他想试探的，是莉雅潜意识里的答案。
因为那个梦，林恩更加确信——自己这位圣女小青梅，恐怕远不像表面那么简单。
“嗯……”莉雅几乎没有犹豫，思考了大概0.5秒便回答，“当然是尝试重新理解啊。”
“但如果身份和力量差距太大，已经脱离底层百姓太久，根本不知道他们在经历什么呢？”
“那就……”莉雅顿了顿，眼神清澈而坚定，“亲自体验一次。”
林恩的嘴角，缓缓扬起了一抹如阳光般明媚，却又意味深长的微笑。
她的灵魂，恐怕真的……非常、非常不简单。
而这一切，她似乎自己也正在试图“理解”。这些。

Chapter 781 Internal Attribution and External Attribution (Page 1)
"Let's start from the inside." Lin En organized his thoughts and tapped his fingertips on the table. "Assuming that subspace can affect reality and give birth to things like monsters and demons, the root causes are often desires and evil thoughts."
"Then it stands to reason that there should be a dynamic balance in the world itself. The power of the 'evil' generated by desire should weaken after it is satisfied - even greed, if over-expanded, will cause backlash, making people around you disgusted and confrontational, thus forming a check and balance."
He paused and looked at Liya: "For example, do you know about sexual desire?"
The tips of Liya's ears were slightly red, and she nodded slightly: "Yes, I know."
"Why are you asking this?" She clasped her hands unconsciously, looking a little embarrassed.
“Lust, that is, sexual desire, when it is satisfied, its drive should weaken because the need has temporarily subsided.”
"The same goes for anger. When the temper is vented, people's emotions will be released, their mood will calm down a lot, and their patience will also increase."
Lynn changed the topic and his eyes became sharp: "So, what will happen in an environment where there are only internal attributions and external attributions are completely eliminated?"
"Whenever something goes wrong, you only doubt yourself?" Liya opened her eyes wide, as if she suddenly touched a blind spot that she had always ignored.
"That's right." Lin En's fingertips tapped a clear rhythm on the table. "Everything is blamed on oneself. Even when the world is 'sick', people still doubt whether it is their own problem, thus falling into endless internal friction."
"But what if the real cause is never found? What if the existing 'treatments' are completely ineffective?"
"Does that mean... we should consider external attribution?"
"In other words, it is completely consistent with the logic and conclusions drawn from our current investigation."
He leaned forward slightly and looked into Liya's eyes:
"Those who look and sound like you...may not be human at all. Instead, they are existences like 'orcs' - they are completely different from you in terms of soul structure."
"But if you think 'everyone is the same' and just see it as a simple 'evil person', then what do you suspect?"
"What you suspect is still a problem within the same race."
"The same goes for magnifying this logic to the world level. Assuming that there really is a law of 'emotions affecting reality' in the world——"
"So, when everyone thinks that 'it was their own fault that caused all this,' what can the race, individual, or some kind of will that deliberately creates this contradiction get from it?"
The victim is completely unaware that the problem lies outside, but constantly blames himself, thinking that everything is his fault. "
"That is to say... Judging from your dream and my deduction, should we re-examine - the 'alien' identity of the Abyssal Tribe may be far more 'alien' than we imagined? "
“Then, there’s the gods, Leah. He recalled the gods in those records, "You said that gods are the embodiment of concepts, and their authority is closely connected with concepts." "
“But what if the concept itself is contaminated and distorted? Isn’t this how the evil god was born? "
At least, that seems to be the case with the fall of the "god of love".
"Liya, you said..." Lin En asked a probing question, but observed her reaction deeply, "If a god wants to 'return to normal', what should he do? "
The one he wanted to test was Liya.The subconscious answer.
Because of that dream, Lin En was even more convinced that this little saintly girl of hers might not be as simple as she appeared.
"Well..." Liya almost didn't hesitate. She thought for about 0.5 seconds before answering, "Of course I'm trying to understand it again."
"But what if the gap in identity and power is too big, and you have been separated from the lower class people for too long, and you don't even know what they are going through?"
"Then..." Liya paused, her eyes clear and firm, "experience it for yourself."
The corner of Lin En's mouth slowly raised into a smile as bright as the sun, but also meaningful.
Her soul, I'm afraid, is really... very, very extraordinary.
And she seems to be trying to "understand" all of this. These.
